facts.claim: Notion's hosted MCP server (streamable HTTP, recommended) is at /mcp
MCP host and OAuth issuer/authorize/token/register endpoints are all on mcp.notion.com
facts.evidence: Discovery document: issuer https://mcp.notion.com; authorize, token and register on the same host.

facts.claim: No scopes are documented; discovery lists only 'default'; template leaves scopes empty so the server decides
facts.evidence: scopes_supported: default; docs page names no scopes.

facts.claim: Dynamic client registration is offered, so no OAuth app has to be created first; OAuth is the only documented method
facts.evidence: registration_endpoint https://mcp.notion.com/register; docs: requires you to complete the OAuth authorization flow.

facts.claim: notion-get-self returns the connected workspace and user and takes no arguments
facts.evidence: Call with an empty object (supported-tools page).

facts.claim: notion-delete-pages and notion-delete-databases move items to Trash and are marked destructive
facts.evidence: Move up to 20 pages to Trash; requires user_confirmed.

facts.claim: @notionhq/notion-mcp-server (stdio, bearer integration token) latest is 2.5.2 and is no longer actively maintained; Notion calls it a last resort
facts.evidence: README: no longer actively maintained; registry latest 2.5.2 (registry.npmjs.org/@notionhq/notion-mcp-server).

choices.because: Notion documents browser OAuth only for its hosted server and discovery advertises dynamic registration; the open-source package is unmaintained.
No scopes documented; discovery shows only 'default'.
Supported-tools page lists it as a no-argument read.

open: The /mcp path rests on one vendor page (the discovery document confirms host only).
The docs state no plan requirement; workspace owners manage client access under Settings > Connections (one page).
Whether sign-in sends the browser to hosts other than mcp.notion.com (e.g. a notion.so login) is not documented; network.hosts lists only the MCP host and connect may refuse if another is needed.
Tool names come from the supported-tools page (39 tools); it was not cross-checked against the live tools/list.
No policy.consent could be set: the mcp-oauth kind rejects connect.policy.
